text: Core-gene frequency varies by fitness category, from 82% among 27,693 essential genes to 66% among 94,889 always-neutral genes; the table gives counts and percentages for all six categories.
quote:
| Essential (no viable mutants) | 27,693 | **82%** |
| Often sick (>10% experiments) | 15,989 | 78% |
| Mixed (sick + beneficial) | 20,739 | 70% |
| Sometimes sick | 25,201 | 72% |
| Always neutral | 94,889 | **66%** |
| Sometimes beneficial | 9,705 | 70% |
heading: Conservation Increases with Fitness Importance

text: Binning by strongest fitness effect gives 82.2% core for essential genes, 77.7% for min_fit < -3, and 66.4% for min_fit -1 to 0.
quote: The same gradient holds when binning by strongest fitness effect: essential -> 82.2% core, min_fit < -3 -> 77.7%, min_fit -1 to 0 -> 66.4%.

text: Deletion is ever beneficial for 24.4% of core genes versus 19.9% of auxiliary genes (OR=0.77 for auxiliary versus core), contrary to an expectation that accessory genes are more burdensome.
quote: Counter to the expectation that accessory genes might be costly to carry, **core genes are MORE likely to show positive fitness effects** when deleted (24.4% ever beneficial vs 19.9% for auxiliary, OR=0.77 for auxiliary vs core).
heading: Core Genes Are Not Burdens -- They're More Likely Beneficial

text: Condition-dependent trade-offs are proposed as a possible explanation for beneficial effects of some core-gene deletions, not established as their cause.
quote: This may reflect that core genes are more likely to participate in trade-off situations -- they help in some conditions but cost in others.

text: Genes tagged with strong condition-specific effects are 77.3% core versus 70.3% for genes without specific phenotypes (OR=1.78, p=1.8e-97).
quote: Genes with strong condition-specific effects (tagged in `specificphenotype`) are 77.3% core vs 70.3% for genes without specific phenotypes (OR=1.78, p=1.8e-97).
heading: Specific-Phenotype Genes Are More Likely Core

text: The observed condition-specific-phenotype result runs counter to the expectation that these genes would preferentially be accessory.
quote: This contradicts the naive expectation that condition-specific genes would be accessory.
heading: Specific-Phenotype Genes Are More Likely Core

text: Participation in well-characterized pathways is offered only as a possible explanation for more measurable condition-specific effects among core genes.
quote: Instead, it suggests that core genes are more likely to have measurable condition-specific effects -- perhaps because they participate in well-characterized pathways.

text: The report identifies 4,450 genes (2.7%) as neutral overall but critical in one condition, its "ephemeral niche gene" pattern.
quote: 4,450 genes (2.7%) fit the "ephemeral niche gene" pattern: neutral overall but critical in one condition.
heading: Ephemeral Niche Genes

text: The ephemeral-niche pattern occurs in 3.0% of core genes, 1.7% of auxiliary genes, and 1.6% of singleton genes.
quote: Surprisingly, these are MORE common in core genes (3.0%) than auxiliary (1.7%) or singleton (1.6%).
heading: Ephemeral Niche Genes

text: Greater detectability of conditional effects is proposed as a possible, rather than demonstrated, explanation for the core-gene enrichment.
quote: Core genes may simply have more detectable conditional effects because they participate in more pathways.

quote: Core and auxiliary genes show distinct fitness effect distributions, with core genes having heavier tails in both the negative (important) and positive (burdensome) directions.

quote: ![Novel Gene Mean Fitness](figures/novel_gene_mean_fitness.png)
heading: Novel Gene Landscape

text: Novel singleton genes have near-zero mean fitness under tested laboratory conditions; the report interprets this as limited assay visibility rather than evidence of systematic benefit or harm.
quote: Novel (singleton) genes show near-zero mean fitness, suggesting they are largely invisible to lab-based fitness assays -- neither beneficial nor detrimental under tested conditions.
heading: Novel Gene Landscape

text: Across ~194,000 genes in 43 bacteria, the report describes a 16-percentage-point core-frequency difference between essential genes (82%) and always-neutral genes (66%).
quote: The results paint a consistent picture: **gene fitness importance and pangenome conservation are positively correlated across the full spectrum**. Essential genes are 82% core; always-neutral genes are 66% core. This 16-percentage-point gradient spans ~194,000 genes across 43 diverse bacteria.
heading: Interpretation

text: The report interprets larger effects in both directions among core genes as suggesting greater functional activity under laboratory conditions; the proposed pathway explanation is inferential.
quote: These patterns suggest that core genes are the most functionally active genes -- they have the largest fitness effects in both directions because they're embedded in critical pathways. Accessory genes, by contrast, tend to be functionally quieter under lab conditions.
heading: Interpretation

text: The report attributes the Fitness Browser data to Price et al. (2018) and says this analysis adds pangenome conservation information to those fitness measurements.
quote: - **Price et al. (2018)** generated the Fitness Browser data used here, providing the largest resource of genome-wide mutant fitness data for bacteria. Our analysis adds a pangenome conservation dimension to their fitness measurements.
heading: Literature Context

text: As literature context, the report cites Luo et al. (2015) for stronger purifying selection on core than accessory genes.
quote: - **Luo et al. (2015)** showed that core genes have stronger purifying selection than accessory genes across bacterial species, consistent with our finding that genes with stronger fitness effects are more likely core.
heading: Literature Context

text: As literature context, the report attributes a selection–drift–HGT account of pangenome gene frequencies to McInerney et al. (2017) and interprets its own gradient as support for selection in core-gene maintenance.
quote: - **McInerney et al. (2017)** reviewed the gene-sharing network view of pangenomes, arguing that gene frequency distributions reflect a balance of selection, drift, and HGT. Our fitness-conservation gradient provides empirical support for selection as a major driver of core gene maintenance.
heading: Literature Context

text: The assayed laboratory conditions favor rich media and standard stresses and do not represent many ecological niches.
quote: - Lab conditions are biased toward rich media and standard stresses; many ecological niches are unrepresented
heading: Limitations

text: Despite the statistically robust 16pp gradient, fitness importance weakly predicts conservation.
quote: - The 16pp gradient, while statistically robust, means conservation is only weakly predicted by fitness importance
heading: Limitations

text: Single-gene knockout fitness measurements do not capture epistatic interactions.
quote: - Fitness measurements are for single-gene knockouts; epistatic interactions are not captured
heading: Limitations

text: The Fitness Browser sample covers 43 bacteria, primarily Proteobacteria, limiting generalizability.
quote: - The Fitness Browser covers 43 bacteria -- primarily Proteobacteria -- limiting generalizability
heading: Limitations

text: Poor transposon coverage could explain missing fitness data for novel singleton genes; near-zero observed fitness should not automatically be treated as true neutrality.
quote: - Singleton/novel genes may lack fitness data due to poor transposon coverage rather than true neutrality
heading: Limitations
